requirements.reason: The Space segment table and immediately following revenue paragraph explicitly give the 2025-versus-2024 increase of $290 million (7.6%), relatively flat Launch Services revenue, and the $298 million increase in Launch and Development. The same paragraph identifies both principal drivers: an extended NASA contract for additional CRS missions and a U.S. Department of War contract.

citations.quote:
Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $290 million, or 7.6%, compared to the prior year 
ended December 31, 2024.  Launch Services revenue remained relatively flat year over year, while Launch and 
Development revenue increased by $298 million.  The Launch and Development revenue increase was primarily 
driven by increased revenue for an extended contract with NASA for additional Cargo Resupply Services (CRS) 
missions to the International Space Station and increased revenue from a U.S. Department of War contract.

requirements.reason: The Cost of Revenue paragraph directly states the $189 million (12.2%) decrease for 2025 versus 2024 and links it to greater Falcon reusability, a $240 million reduction in the expense described by the source as “deprecation,” and $11 million lower overhead. Direction, amounts, comparison period and the causal links are explicit; the source spelling is retained in the quote.

citations.quote:
Cost of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $189 million, or 12.2%, compared to the prior 
year ended December 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily due increased reusability of our Falcon launch vehicles 
resulting in lower deprecation of $240 million, lowering the cost of each launch, and lower overhead costs of $11 
million.

requirements.reason: The continuation explicitly reports Starlink launches rising from 89 in 2024 to 122 in 2025, $14 million more launch-operation and overhead costs capitalized in the company’s Connectivity segment, and a $51 million increase in excess/obsolescence inventory reserves partly offsetting the decrease. It connects the launch shift to capitalization and distinguishes the offset from the cost-reducing drivers.

citations.quote:
The decrease is also due to the relative increase in Starlink satellite launches from 89 launches in 2024 to 
122 launches in 2025, resulting in relatively more of our launch operations and overhead costs capitalized in our 
Connectivity segment of $14 million.  This decrease was partially offset by an increase in inventory excess and 
obsolescence reserves of $51 million mainly due to less demand on rocket vehicle and spacecraft parts as reusability 
has increased.
